name: SciMiner 1.1 & 2.0
description: Web-based literature mining tool for gene/protein extraction and functional enrichment analysis.

details.longDescription: SciMiner is a web-based literature mining and functional analysis tool that automatically identifies genes and proteins mentioned in biomedical text. It processes PubMed abstracts or user-supplied text to extract gene/protein mentions using dictionary-based and rule-based NLP approaches, then performs functional enrichment analysis (Gene Ontology, KEGG pathways) on the extracted targets.
features: Automated gene/protein extraction from PubMed abstracts

name: PubChemSR
description: PubChem Search Refined — Python cheminformatics toolkit with CLI, web dashboard, and AI-augmented ADMET prediction.

images.caption: Smart Search with property lookup (AI module)
ADMET predictor with radar chart (AI module)

details.longDescription: PubChemSR is an open-source cheminformatics toolkit for searching, retrieving, and analyzing compound data from NCBI PubChem. The current generation ships three coordinated interfaces: a scriptable Python library plus CLI (pubchemsr) for batch workflows, an interactive web dashboard (pubchemsr-web) for point-and-click exploration, and an AI-augmented discovery platform (pubchemsr-ai) that layers ADMET prediction, SAR analysis, and chemical-space visualization on top of the core search engine.
features: Compound search by name, CID, SMILES, InChI, or molecular formula
BioAssay data retrieval and batch processing from CSV/TXT
Drug-likeness filters (Lipinski, Veber, Ghose, Egan, Muegge)
ADMET prediction, SAR analysis, and chemical-space visualization (AI module)
Export to CSV, Excel, JSON, and SDF formats

name: ChemFuse
description: Multi-database cheminformatics suite integrating PubChem, ChEMBL, UniChem, BindingDB, Open Targets, and SureChEMBL.

details.longDescription: ChemFuse unifies compound search, ADMET prediction, and cross-database identifier mapping into a single coherent API. A single function call searches PubChem, ChEMBL, UniChem, BindingDB, Open Targets, and SureChEMBL in parallel, merges the results by structure, and returns a unified compound collection. From there, ChemFuse computes 200+ molecular descriptors, applies drug-likeness filters, predicts ADMET properties via ML models, clusters compounds in chemical space, and exports the merged dataset — all from Python, R, the command line, or a Streamlit dashboard.
features: Parallel async queries across 6 public chemistry databases
No API keys required for any integrated source
200+ RDKit descriptors and Lipinski / Veber / Ghose / Egan / Muegge filters
ML-based ADMET prediction (solubility, BBB, CYP, hepatotoxicity, etc.)
Local SQLite cache with TTL + LRU eviction
Python package, R package (via reticulate), CLI, Streamlit dashboard, Docker

name: DNMKB2
description: Repository and analysis portal for diabetic neuropathy transcriptomics data with 140 DEG sets.

details.longDescription: DNMKB2 (Diabetic Neuropathy Molecular Knowledge Base v2) is a comprehensive repository and analysis portal for diabetic peripheral neuropathy transcriptomics data. It integrates 140 differentially expressed gene (DEG) sets from multiple DPN studies, enabling cross-study comparison, meta-analysis, and pathway enrichment across mouse and human models.

name: VennDetail
description: Bioconductor R package for Venn-Pie plots and subset extraction supporting up to 8 sets.

images.caption: Venn-Pie and bar-plot views of overlapping gene sets

details.longDescription: VennDetail is a Bioconductor R package that provides comprehensive Venn diagram analysis with Pie chart overlays. Unlike traditional Venn diagrams limited to 3-4 sets, VennDetail supports up to 8 sets and provides detailed subset extraction, making it ideal for comparing gene lists from multiple omics experiments.
features: Support for up to 8 comparison sets

name: richR
description: Functional enrichment and visualization R package for comprehensive pathway analysis.

details.longDescription: richR is a comprehensive R package for functional enrichment analysis supporting GO, KEGG, Reactome, and custom gene sets. It provides advanced visualization including dot plots, bar plots, network plots, and enrichment maps, with built-in support for multiple species and gene ID conversion.
features: Multiple visualization types (dot, bar, network, enrichment map)

name: Tox21 Enricher
description: Online enrichment tool for Tox21 chemical screening data with R version available.

details.longDescription: Tox21 Enricher is an online tool for performing enrichment analysis on Tox21 chemical screening data from the NIH Tox21 program. It allows researchers to identify overrepresented biological pathways and toxicity endpoints among sets of chemical compounds, supporting both web-based and R package interfaces.
features: Enrichment analysis for Tox21 chemical data

name: richStudio
description: R Shiny application for interactive enrichment and clustering analyses.

details.longDescription: richStudio is an interactive R Shiny web application that provides a GUI for performing enrichment analysis and hierarchical clustering without writing code. It wraps richR and richCluster functionality in an accessible web interface for researchers with limited programming experience.

name: richCluster
description: C++-based hierarchical clustering algorithm wrapped in R for high-performance cluster analysis.

details.longDescription: richCluster is an R package with a C++ backend that provides high-performance hierarchical clustering for large-scale biological data. It implements optimized algorithms for gene expression clustering, pathway grouping, and enrichment result organization, significantly outperforming pure R implementations.

name: scGEN
description: Gene-aware embedding network for single-cell RNA-seq clustering using deep learning.

images.caption: scGEN framework overview (Figure 1 of the scGEN paper, Advanced Science)

details.longDescription: scGEN (single-cell Gene-aware Embedding Network) is a deep learning framework for single-cell RNA-seq analysis. It uses gene-aware neural network architectures to learn biologically meaningful cell embeddings, enabling improved cell type clustering, trajectory inference, and batch effect correction compared to traditional dimensionality reduction methods.

name: DPNKB
description: Revamped successor to DNMKB2: a comprehensive knowledgebase integrating genomic, transcriptomic, and clinical data for diabetic peripheral neuropathy research.

details.longDescription: DPNKB (Diabetic Peripheral Neuropathy Knowledge Base) is a comprehensive web-based knowledgebase that integrates genomic, transcriptomic, and clinical data for the study of diabetic peripheral neuropathy (DPN). It serves as an exploration and analysis platform for DPN gene expression data, enabling researchers to query and analyze differentially expressed genes across multiple DPN studies and models.

name: VIOLIN
description: Vaccine Investigation and Online Information Network — a comprehensive vaccine knowledgebase integrating AI-driven literature analysis with ontology annotation.

details.longDescription: VIOLIN (Vaccine Investigation and Online Information Network) is a comprehensive web-based vaccine knowledgebase that integrates AI-driven literature analysis with ontology-based data annotation. VIOLIN 2.0 includes curated data on vaccine components, host responses, and protection mechanisms across hundreds of licensed and experimental vaccines, supported by the Vaccine Ontology (VO) for standardized representation.
features: Host response and protection mechanism data

name: Ignet
description: Interactive gene interaction network visualization and analysis system for ontology-based literature-mined networks.

details.longDescription: Ignet is an interactive web-based system for visualizing and analyzing gene-gene interaction networks derived from ontology-based literature mining. It displays networks extracted by SciMiner and other NLP tools, allowing researchers to explore gene relationships, identify hub genes, and discover novel biological connections in the published literature.

name: Vignet
description: Vaccine-focused integrative gene network: vaccine–gene interaction networks mined from PubMed literature and mapped to the Vaccine Ontology.

details.longDescription: Vignet (Vaccine-focused Integrative Gene Network) is the vaccine-first view into the same literature-mining data that powers Ignet. Where Ignet is organized around genes, Vignet is organized around vaccines, using the terms of the Vaccine Ontology (VO). Researchers can build vaccine–gene–drug–disease networks, find the vaccines most associated with a gene list, compare vaccines side by side, and ask vaccine-specific questions with PMID-grounded answers. It currently covers 645 vaccines, 3,242 linked genes, and 253,431 PubMed articles.
features: Browse and profile 600+ vaccines mined from PubMed
Vaccine–gene pair evidence and co-occurrence sentences
Vaccine enrichment from a user gene list
AI literature assistant with PMID-grounded answers

name: AURORA
description: NIH-style asynchronous peer review of grant applications: 1–9 criterion scoring, anonymous reviewer discussion, and study-section report export.

details.longDescription: AURORA (Asynchronous Unified Review Of Research Applications) is a web platform for NIH-style peer review of grant applications. Administrators organize review cycles, study sections, and reviewer assignments; reviewers score each NIH criterion on the 1–9 scale, write structured strengths and weaknesses, and discuss applications anonymously (as Reviewer A, B, C) without needing a synchronous meeting. Accounts are invite-only through the study-section administrator.
features: Review cycles, study sections, and reviewer assignment
Structured NIH criteria form with 1–9 scoring
Reviewer and administrator dashboards with progress tracking
Application statistics by status, study section, and grant type

name: Research PDF Renamer
description: Renames research PDFs to Author_Year_Journal_Keywords using LLM-extracted bibliographic metadata.

details.longDescription: Research PDF Renamer replaces unhelpful file names such as document.pdf or 1-s2.0-S0123456789.pdf with consistent, descriptive names. It uses a large language model to extract the author, year, title, journal, and keywords from the first pages of each paper, then renames the files and returns them for download. It supports OpenAI, Ollama, LM Studio, and other OpenAI-compatible servers, so it can run fully locally. The hosted version requires the UND network and an approved account.
features: LLM extraction of author, year, title, journal, and keywords
OpenAI, Ollama, LM Studio, or any OpenAI-compatible server
Privacy-first: only text from the first 1–2 pages is sent; files deleted after download
Registration with admin approval and usage tracking
Docker, systemd + Apache, or standalone Flask deployment

name: IRB Assistant
description: AI-assisted drafting of HRP-503, HRP-503c, and HRP-398 IRB forms from uploaded study documents.

details.longDescription: IRB Assistant helps researchers draft three IRB protocol forms from their study documents: HRP-503 (full Human Research Protocol), HRP-503c (Human Research Engagement Determination), and HRP-398 (AI Considerations Worksheet). Creating a Study sets up all three submissions; uploaded documents are shared across them and drive an AI first pass that proposes answers with evidence quotes for the researcher to review before exporting filled DOCX files. It is being piloted at the University of North Dakota with Sanford Health, funded by NIH/NIGMS through TRANSCEND.
features: One Study creates all three form submissions
AI first-pass answers grounded in evidence quotes
Review and edit every suggested answer
Export filled DOCX files for IRB submission

name: UND Co.AI
description: Checks research proposals, grant applications, and project documents against UND, NDUS, state, and federal AI guidelines.

details.longDescription: UND Co.AI is an AI compliance checker for UND researchers, faculty, and graduate students. Users upload a document such as an IRB proposal, grant application, course redesign, or syllabus and receive an automated analysis of its AI use against federal, research-ethics, North Dakota state, NDUS, UND, and department policies. Each finding comes with a plain-English description, a severity rating, a recommended action, and the relevant UND office to contact; reports can be downloaded as PDF for IRB or grant submissions.
features: Federal guidance: NIST AI RMF, FERPA, HIPAA, OMB M-25-21
Research ethics and grant rules: NIH, NSF PAPPG, ORI, ICMJE
North Dakota, NDUS, and UND AI policies
Plain-English findings with severity and recommended action

name: SMHS Publication Atlas
description: Interactive dashboard of UND School of Medicine & Health Sciences publications, collaborations, and research strengths.

details.longDescription: The SMHS Publication Atlas shows where the UND School of Medicine & Health Sciences' research strengths lie, who is building them together, and who is publishing alone. It currently covers 1,764 publications by 1,052 named SMHS authors across 34 units (2020–2026). Every view responds to the year, department, and topic filters, and each count states its unit.
features: Filters by year, department, topic, and free-text search
Strength map and teams by research area

name: NDResHub
description: Turns a plain-language research idea into ranked North Dakota experts, resources, and potential collaborators.

details.longDescription: NDResHub (ND Research Hub) helps researchers find the right experts, resources, and collaborators for a research idea. A plain-language description of the idea is matched against North Dakota publications, grants, and people, and each ranked match shows the reasoning behind it. It currently indexes 43,717 people, 25,023 publications, and 366 grants, serving UND researchers and, on the data side, statewide institutions.
features: Semantic researcher–grant matching with visible reasoning
Grants from NIH RePORTER, NSF, and USAspending.gov
Browsable people, publications, grants, and resources
